title: Mocks, stubs and the small interface that makes them easy

videos.script: Real code opens files and talks to servers. A test that does the same is slow, and it fails for reasons that have nothing to do with your code. {{seam}} The Go answer is not a framework. It is a small interface, with one method, declared by the code that needs it. The package gains a function that counts a document by name, and asks only for something that can open one. {{doubles}} Then three stand-ins, each a few lines of plain Go. A fake that keeps documents in a map. A stub that always fails. And a spy that takes notes. {{spy}} The spy finds a defect no return value shows: the function never closes what it opens. One line fixes it. {{real}} Last, what not to replace. A reader, a buffer, a file system in memory: the real thing is cheap, so you use it. {{close}} Lesson 28 tests the other side of the seam, against a real server.
